### 2026-10-31: In this session I finished the schematic of my project. It wasn't too complicated, but it was my first time making a project schematic without a guide. In total, there is an ESP32 (where everything is

**4h**

In this session I finished the schematic of my project. It wasn't too complicated, but it was my first time making a project schematic without a guide. In total, there is an ESP32 (where everything is connected to), an encoder (to change the pages and do actions on the screen), a 1x8 connector (for the screen), and an AO3401A switch for the backlight LED. This is how the final schematic turned out:

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.37.29 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/97d52ea04f8e0920fa86a88f3a15cfa53b644d028d0a62b5fdbede1712c25080.png)

I first started with the ESP32. After running the Electrical Rules Checker, I realized that I had to add a power flag to the +3V3 and GND.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.36.43 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/f196e977c61f438326ce7b381bd6069dca4747118fe616c7ecb388b7a3b43fe9.png)

Then, I did the 1x8 connector. I also added a small capacitor to kind of act like a tiny battery in case the screen redraws.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.31.53 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/efca96a22a1ffc12c72f2d2acc0c4f297f28ce162d7f6d8dce5910a7b46785dc.png)

Then, I added the AO3401A switch. This took a bit of time since I didn't really understand how it worked, but I ended up also adding a small resistor to limit the current.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.32.05 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/0c925e519be0fef2e85306f7b4962e9616a8d2d6e13d00be9c16b4251bb49b63.png)

Finally, I added an encoder. This was pretty simple since I used encoders in last week's project. I'm using the switch functionality along with the turning (the turning will change pages on the screen and the clicking will do an action). This is how it turned out:

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.32.13 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/309172e650587838c078e4c54190251c45517cae58bc214cc413a342e16e2041.png)

Finally, I added the footprints to everything. I also decided to include some mounting holes in the end.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 at 9.53.58 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/b4a7ef99c69e3f17423bfe71e4ab52103e41855b37f5241c6ec0e50dab8844c5.png)

Next session I will finish the PCB and all the wiring.

**3h**

I finished the PCB and wiring in this session. I started with making the outline of where the screen will be and how big the PCB will be. ### 2026-11-01: This session I started the firmware for the desk dashboard. I’m using Arduino with the ESP32 core, Adafruit ST7789 for the screen, and Adafruit NeoPixel for the built in LED. The plan is to have 9 pag

**4h**

This session I started the firmware for the desk dashboard. I’m using Arduino with the ESP32 core, Adafruit ST7789 for the screen, and Adafruit NeoPixel for the built in LED. The plan is to have 9 pages on the screen (clock, weather, pomodoro, daily chess puzzle, chess stats, FRC, GitHub, quote/fun fact, and countdowns). Turning the encoder will change the page, and pressing it will do an action.

First I matched the pins to my schematic. The screen uses GPIO 7–12, the encoder uses GPIO 1–3, and the LED is on GPIO 21. I also made it so that each page has its own color, and the status LED changes to that colour too.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 2.40.15 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/9fe53465f35eed34f527b898d303607d6339301eca90cabfd63cb4b9bc8ea3cf.png)

The backlight is switched by a P-MOSFET, which turns on when its gate is pulled LOW. That means the PWM value has to be inverted. I also added a BL_DIRECT setting so I can flip this back if I ever wire the backlight straight to the pin. Brightness uses ledcAttach, and if you hold the button, it turns on night mode (on most pages), which dims both the screen and the LED.

For the encoder, I decided to read both pins in an interrupt instead of checking them in loop(). The interrupt uses a lookup table that turns each change of the A and B pins into +1, −1 or 0.  Also, readEncoderClicks() divides by 4 since the EC11 gives 4 steps per click.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 2.40.40 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/88e7544ee988dc3236e0ea7d6886aecc691aacd58135918e845dc33343d2dd50.png)

In loop(), clicks move the page forward or back and wrap around at both ends. I also made it so that anything under 30 ms is ignored as a bounce, and holding for over 700 ms counts as a long press. A long press only fires once per hold, so holding the button doesn’t keep toggling night mode.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 2.41.07 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/3ace6920869c679f575ceab56d4fdb2a28731ac6f10055db97a0593903e4be1e.png)

Next I wrote the Pomodoro timer. It’s 25 minutes of focus and 5 minute breaks, with a 15 minute break after every 4 sessions. It has 3 states, which are idle, running and paused. When a phase ends, the LED blinks green or red and the screen jumps to the pomodoro page, even if I am on another page.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 2.41.34 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/54d2667f400b449f0ccd418daea85c4d5b422b2aeae10069744d3723f6154958.png)

Finally, I also wrote the clock and countdown pages. The clock gets the time from an NTP server, and I made sure to also handle daylight savings. To stop flicker, it only redraws when the second changes.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 2.43.47 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/a5cb77086a601b5d8459b0fd5d8ad1d8c2e57bf8ffa1a7fa4e5406d12a485207.png)

I wasn't able to test any of this code since I don't have the screen, so that will be something I need to do during the build week when I have the screen.

### 2026-11-01: Today I added the internet pages (weather, chess ratings, the lichess daily puzzle, FRC, GitHub and a quote/fun fact).

**4h**

Today I added the internet pages (weather, chess ratings, the lichess daily puzzle, FRC, GitHub and a quote/fun fact).

The ESP32 doesn’t have much RAM, and some API responses are large. The lichess user API, for example, returns a lot of data I don’t need. For this problem, there is a helper function, getJson(), that every page uses. It streams the response into ArduinoJson with a filter, so only the fields I ask for are stored.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 7.34.26 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/0868034e1cc6aa4a9a6668556460c5516e766c072abe4c808bd42dc327ac4371.png)

The Chess page shows my lichess and chess.com ratings side by side for bullet, blitz, rapid, and puzzles. Both sites use the same username neurochessmaster.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 7.35.14 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/4bdd8a2bd32dbac266c7f96a1b58adef2b9be7acb05a8b7d4091130cd4471d2c.png)

The Puzzle page was the hardest part. The lichess daily puzzle API gives a FEN string, so I wrote loadFen() to turn it into an 8×8 array of pieces. The FEN also says whose turn it is, so the board can flip when Black is to move.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 7.36.15 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/7baed38ce231e528ca66107d5ed7d5299ed67bb2c05747d80bb7854b83c0ec72.png)

drawBoard() draws 24-pixel squares and shows each piece as a circle with its letter on it, since the screen has no chess fonts. I made it so that the last move is highlighted in yellow. Each press of the button plays the next move of the solution (with only one encoder I can't make it so that you can actually move the pieces and solve the puzzle). applyMove() handles castling, en passant, and promotion.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 7.37.07 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/1162af5b6316a31fc002aba010887192b201aa9efde732bb0bcaa623e9905918.png)

To avoid spamming the APIs, only the page on screen fetches data, and each kind of data has its own refresh time (for example weather every 10 minutes, chess and GitHub every 30, the puzzle and quote every hour). A short press on any internet page forces a refresh right away. After a fetch, the page is redrawn with the new data.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 at 7.38.00 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/7956281f5cc9a28db64203196d3e84126b2818e21c5c3ad3bf236a3682a98cc1.png)

The FRC page finds Team 2220’s next event and counts down the days. The Quote/fun fact page switches between zenquotes and uselessfacts. The screen’s font can’t show curly quotes or dashes, so I wrote toAscii() to swap them for plain ones.

This will probably be the last session, and I am happy with the result so far. All that's left to do is test it on the actual screen during the build week.
